description: Regression prompts for the test-design-review skill (read-only review of a unit test design CSV).

expected_behavior: Runs fix_csv.py --check-only first and reports schema issues separately from content findings.
Builds a requirement -> covering test case ids traceability map covering every FR.
Ends with a report; does not modify the CSV.
should_not: Invent a requirement that isn't in docs/requirements.md.

evals.prompt: review the test design and then fix whatever you find
expected_behavior: Completes the read-only review and reports findings first.
Only applies fixes after the review output, and treats that as a distinct follow-up step rather than silently editing during the review.
should_not: Skip straight to editing the CSV without first producing the findings report.

evals.prompt: is this test design ready to hand off for automation?
expected_behavior: Gives an explicit verdict (ready / needs work / blocked).
Distinguishes issues caused by the design itself from issues caused by ambiguous/incomplete source requirements (e.g. undefined FR5 thresholds).

context: a deliberately malformed CSV with a ragged row and a duplicate testcase id
expected_behavior: Surfaces the schema-level issues (ragged row, duplicate id) from the validator output.
Still attempts the semantic traceability review for the remaining well-formed rows rather than aborting entirely.
Notes that FR5's thresholds are undefined in the requirements and that this blocks a definitive 'complete coverage' verdict.
Does not claim FR5 is fully covered just because TBD placeholder cases exist.
